item.title: When Coupling Backfires: BBR-Induced L4S Degradation under DualPI2
item.description: arXiv:2611.31634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low Latency, Low Loss, Scalable Throughput (L4S) uses DualPI2 to separate low latency (e.g., TCP Prague) and Classic flows into two queues while coupling their congestion signals. However, this coupling is designed for Reno-like Classic congestion controls, while widely deployed BBR behaves differently. Prior studies observed severe Prague throughput degradation when BBR occupies the Classic queue under DualPI2, but the mechanism remains insufficiently explained. Through controlled testbed experiments and an extension of an existing BBRv1/BBRv2 fluid model with PI2, we show that BBR can drive the PI2 base probability p' far above CUBIC levels, producing strong coupled marking that can nearly starve Prague despite low L4S queueing delay. The model explains BBRv1's persistent high-p' regime, BBRv2's lower, oscillating p', and their dependence on the PI2 target relative to RTT. Additional experiments show that Prague throughput degradation also occurs with BBRv3. Our findings highlight the need for coupling mechanisms supporting low latency flows across heterogeneous Classic congestion controls.
item.dc:creator: Fatih Berkay Sarpkaya, Fraida Fund, Shivendra Panwar

item.title: Inference-Aware Congestion Control for Distributed MoE Inference
item.description: arXiv:2611.32083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Congestion control is central to low-latency datacenter communication, yet link utilization and queue state do not reveal whether delivered bytes advance an application. This distinction matters in distributed mixture-of-experts (MoE) inference: collective transfers jointly satisfy GPU dependencies, while computation may overlap with communication. The transfer limiting a consumer can therefore change over time, and extra bandwidth may have little effect while that consumer is still computing. We study this interaction and present IACC, which combines ACK/INT feedback with collective and consumer progress when allocating QP rates. A fixed-snapshot analysis characterizes budget conservation and weighted max-min allocation. Across five trace-guided workloads at baseline arrival density, IACC lowers mean TTFT and TPOT relative to HPCC by 6.32%-19.41% and 7.02%-27.33%, respectively. Across tested workload-density settings through 1.25x, mean and p95 TTFT are also lower.
item.dc:creator: Weiye Chen, Qi Xin, Ahmed M. Abdelmoniem

item.title: Energy and Performance Characterization of UxNBs: Toward AI-Driven Non-Terrestrial Open RAN Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.32258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: UAV-mounted base stations (UxNBs) can provide ondemand 5G coverage, but their limited onboard energy makes power consumption the main operational constraint. AI-driven Open RAN controllers are a promising solution, yet they are trained almost exclusively on analytical models and simulations, since no public dataset captures the real energy behavior of a flying 5G base station (BS). As a first step toward closing this gap, we present a UAV testbed hosting a 5G picocell that supports a 20 MHz carrier and up to 100 Mbps throughput. The testbed measures BS system metrics, including power consumption, CPU load, and temperature, alongside UAV flight telemetry and detailed per-layer vRAN processing metrics. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that jointly exposes the energy and RAN behavior of a flying 5G BS, providing the real measurements needed to train and validate energy-aware AI controllers.

item.title: Operationalizing Quantum Machine Learning for IoT Network Intrusion Detection
item.description: arXiv:2611.32314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has increased networked systems' exposure to cyber threats, making Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs) essential for securing heterogeneous environments. While Deep Learning (DL) has shown strong performance in traffic analysis, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has recently gained attention as an alternative approach to learn complex traffic patterns. We assess QML's practical applicability to intrusion detection in heterogeneous IoT scenarios. We present a hybrid quantum-classical NIDS and evaluate it on three recent IoT security datasets, under operationally relevant conditions. Beyond detection accuracy, we compare QML with a classical DL baseline across five operational perspectives: (i) performance under data scarcity, (ii) transferability through cross-domain evaluation, (iii) resilience to temporal constraints, (iv) robustness to quantum non-idealities across multiple noisy backends, and (v) prediction trustworthiness through calibration analysis. Experiments on binary and multiclass misuse detection show that DL generally outperforms QML under ideal and noisy conditions. However, QML remains competitive in data-scarcity and domain-shift scenarios and can outperform the DL baseline under temporal constraints.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Ciuonzo, Idio Guarino, Alfredo Nascita, Antonio Pescap\`e, Vincenzo Spadari

item.title: Gamification in the age of AI: surveying player perceptions of motivation, manipulation, and data protection
item.description: arXiv:2611.32464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern games and applications increasingly employ artificial intelligence (AI), user modeling, and gamification to influence user behavior, sustain engagement, and monetize attention. Although these mechanisms can enhance motivation and enjoyment, they also raise concerns about manipulation, personal data usage, and transparency. To examine how players perceive these dynamics, we conducted a survey with 28 adult participants. Respondents expressed strong concerns about the collection and exploitation of personal information in games and gamified applications, while also reporting low awareness and a limited sense of control over how their data is used. They evaluated progression features such as leveling systems and leaderboards as motivating. In contrast, they rated retention-focused mechanics such as daily login rewards and random reward reveals as highly manipulative. Participants reported that these systems can create fear of missing out or resemble gambling. Participants also expressed support for regulatory measures that limit exploitative design and protect vulnerable users. These findings reveal a clear gap between increasingly powerful engagement strategies and user trust, illustrating the need for more responsible and transparent gamification practices.
item.dc:creator: Kurt Horvath, Tom Tucek

item.title: Quantum Switches Under Congestion: Stabilization, Scheduling, and Performance
item.description: arXiv:2611.32484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Communications (QC) are set to revolutionize communications by employing and exploiting the properties of quantum systems. In this work, we analyse Quantum Switch Networks (QSN) comprised of quantum switches, both memory-equipped and all-optical switch types, to study the time evolution of the requests' queue lengths and how they behave under certain regimes given by various configurations of the network, all governed by the throughput-optimal, classical MaxWeight Scheduling Policy. The goals of this work are twofold: first, we study the queue length dynamics, evolution and equilibrium under the Fluid Queues Approximation model and as a discrete evolution problem, with the addition of a simple discarding policy that stabilizes any scheduling policy by the introduction of a friction-like term named \textit{discard term} inside the evolution equations. The second goal is the validation of the mechanism by comparing the discrete queue evolution of all-optical and memory-equipped quantum networks under different constraints and complex topologies like BCube and Fat-Tree, which are key topologies present on future Quantum Data Centres.
item.dc:creator: Javier Vecino-Pe\~nas, Manuel Fern\'andez-Veiga, Ana Fern\'andez-Vilas, Rebeca P. D\'iaz-Redondo

item.title: MAQR: Lightweight Memory-Aware Q-Routing for Fresh Status Delivery in Multi-Hop IoBNTs
item.description: arXiv:2611.32661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes memory-aware Q-routing (MAQR) for fresh status delivery over history-dependent molecular links in multi-hop Internet of Bio-Nano Things (IoBNT) networks. Repeated transmissions leave residual molecules, making link reliability history-dependent and fixed routing inefficient. Each link is calibrated from a spatial Markov model and approximated by three nonnegative decay modes. The resulting reduced memory state and packet bit composition provide an instantaneous link-success estimate. MAQR combines quantized memory and reliability descriptors with packet age, queue occupancy, and molecule reserve in a lightweight partially observable Q-routing heuristic. It is trained offline and requires only reduced-state updates and Q-table lookup during deployment. Across five independent training pairs and 20 shared evaluation seeds, MAQR reduces mean AoI by 46.9 % relative to memory-blind Q-routing at 0.30 packets/slot while improving molecular efficiency. Frozen-policy sweeps further show comparable performance under weak memory and an increasing MAQR advantage as channel memory strengthens.
item.dc:creator: Ruifeng Zheng, Veronika Volkova, Zhihan Xu, Pengjie Zhou, Mart\'in Schottlender, Rafael F. Schaefer, Frank H. P. Fitzek, Pit Hofmann

item.title: FugaStream: Pipelined Live Volumetric Streaming towards Full Exploitation of Multi-views
item.description: arXiv:2611.32732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Live volumetric streaming has become the cornerstone of next-generation immersive applications, enabling users to experience six degrees of freedom (6-DoF). To support interactivity, live volumetric streaming must reconstruct multi-view RGB-D frames into a unified 3D representation while meeting a stringent latency budget, where existing systems are forced to trade reconstruction quality for latency. In this paper, we present FugaStream, the first pipelined live volumetric streaming system that mitigates this trade-off by committing a base representation early and then incrementally merging novel late views. Enabling such functionalities introduces two fundamental challenges: (i) the uncertainty in frame availability, and (ii) the late view updates in a lightweight manner. We address these challenges through two key algorithms: (i) adaptive base commitment control, which determines the base commitment time with the expected reconstruction gain of each missing view against the growing cost of latency, and (ii) base-referenced late view completion, which transmits only the novel regions of late views compared to early committed base, enabling lightweight fusion at the client. We validate the effectiveness of FugaStream on a widely used volumetric dataset and a real-world testbed, demonstrating that FugaStream improves SSIM by 10.9% and IoU by 13.7% over baselines under the same 150 ms budget.
item.dc:creator: Edward Jusuk Kim, Huijeong Choe, Minjae Lee, Chanjeong Park, Kyunghan Lee

item.title: Quantization-Induced Performance Degradation in Segment Routing: A Concentration Inequality Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.32838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In segment routing (SR), splitting ratios must be quantized to respect practical hardware precision constraints. Yet no existing work has established an upper bound on the performance degradation caused by such quantization. In this work, we propose source-agnostic systematic rounding, which allows flows sharing a destination to share the same policy, thereby reducing memory consumption, and which approximates the target splitting ratios by a set of power-of-two terms so as to respect the hardware precision limit. We explicitly analyze the consequence of quantizing splitting ratios to integer multiples of 1/64 by a probability-theoretic argument based on concentration inequalities, and we derive an upper bound on the resulting performance degradation. We validate our analysis with extensive experiments on real-world network topologies and flow statistics.
item.dc:creator: Kai Wang, Chee Wei Tan

item.title: Leveraging Persistent Field-of-View and Multipath Segment Routing for Traffic Engineering in LEO Satellite Constellations
item.description: arXiv:2611.32852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations poses fundamental challenges for traditional rout- ing paradigms due to high node mobility, frequent topology changes, and constrained on-board resources. This paper pro- poses a segment routing (SR) framework that offloads route computation and control signaling from resource-constrained LEO switches to more powerful medium earth orbit (MEO) con- trollers. We first establish sufficient conditions for the persistence of user-to-satellite and LEO-to-MEO field-of-view (FoV) con- nectivity throughout a virtual topology (VT) snapshot interval, enabling handover-free operation. Leveraging this persistence, we formulate the MEO control domain partitioning problem as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) to minimize control over- head while assigning disjoint segment routing domains (SRDs) to MEO controllers. Within each SRD, we develop a multipath SR- based traffic engineering (SR-TE) formulation that splits traffic among four minimum-hop-count path types to minimize maxi- mum link utilization. We solve this linear program (LP) using a distributed primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) approach that preserves SRD-level privacy and requires only AllReduce communication. Simulations on the Starlink/GPS combination demonstrate our approach reduces maximum link utilization by more than 13.09%, 11.84%, and 12.50%, respectively, com- pared to traditional minimum hop count routing (MHCR) and traffic-oblivious load-balancing methods for Starlink, Kuiper, and OneWeb.
item.dc:creator: Kai Wang, Chee Wei Tan

item.title: Trustworthy Edge AI: Security, Privacy, and Resilience for Distributed Intelligence
item.description: arXiv:2611.31331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This chapter examines the principles and emerging research directions for building secure, privacy-preserving, and resilient Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) systems. As intelligence shifts from centralized clouds to distributed edge environments, challenges arise in ensuring data integrity, privacy, and reliable operation under adversarial and uncertain conditions. The chapter analyzes Edge AI architectures, emphasizing the expanded attack surface due to heterogeneous devices, resource constraints, and dynamic networks. It reviews core security mechanisms, including hardware-rooted trust, zero-trust models, secure communication, and attestation. Privacy-preserving approaches, such as federated learning, secure aggregation, and differential privacy, enable collaborative intelligence without centralized data sharing. Resilience strategies, including fault tolerance, adversarial robustness, and adaptive orchestration, are also explored. Case studies from smart cities, autonomous vehicles, healthcare, and industrial IoT illustrate practical trade-offs. The chapter advocates a holistic, cross-layer design integrating security, privacy, and resilience for trustworthy edge intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Jaydip Sen, Subhasis Dasgupta

item.title: Wi-Fi Enabled Edge Intelligence Framework for Smart City Traffic Monitoring using Low-Power IoT Cameras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32517v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time traffic monitoring in smart cities demands ultra-low latency processing to support time-critical decisions such as incident detection and congestion management. While cloud-based solutions offer robust computation, their inherent latency limits their applicability for such tasks. This work proposes a localized edge AI framework that connects low-power IoT camera sensors to a client, or applies offloading of inference to an NVIDIA Jetson Nano (GPU). Networking is achieved via Wi-Fi, enabling image classification without relying on wide-area infrastructure such as 5G, or wired networks. We evaluate two processing strategies: local inference on camera nodes and GPU-accelerated offloading to the Jetson Nano.We show that local processing is only feasible for lightweight models and low frame rates, whereas offloading enables near-realtime performance even for more complex models. These results demonstrate the viability of cost-effective, Wi-Fi-based edge AI deployments for latency-critical urban monitoring.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Walcher, Kurt Horvath, Dragi Kimovski, Stojan Kitanov

item.title: Embodied Intelligence for Spectrum Map Construction in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.32799v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate spectrum map construction by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for intelligent resource management in low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs). Although various construction approaches have been investigated, their performance often degrades under extremely sparse sampling because purely data-driven models may not capture the underlying propagation physics. To address these challenges, an embodied intelligence framework is proposed, which synergistically integrates closed-loop perception-cognition-execution (PCE) coupling and embodied exploration to achieve precise and efficient spectrum construction. Based on this framework, a corresponding embodied cognition and decision network (ECDNet) with three tightly coupled modules is designed. Specifically, by leveraging distance-aware convolutions, the semantic bridge, and adaptive feature alignment mechanisms, ECDNet establishes the bidirectional information flow between construction and decision-making. Simulation results show that ECDNet achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.787 dBm at 4.00% sampling under the non-revisiting spiral protocol. Furthermore, a practical UAV-based spectrum construction platform is developed and field-deployed to provide prototype-level evidence that the sensing, cognition, and action modules execute as a closed loop on size, weight, and power constrained UAV edge devices.
item.dc:creator: Hongtao Liang, Yiyao Wan, Jiahuan Ji, Lingda Meng, Fuhui Zhou, Qihui Wu

item.title: Towards Energy- and QoS-aware Load Balancing for 5G Advanced: Leveraging O-RAN to Achieve Sustainability and Energy Efficiency
item.description: arXiv:2503.13726v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The increasing energy consumption of next-generation mobile networks necessitates the adoption of autonomous and energy-aware management strategies. This article proposes a novel adaptive solution leveraging the Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture to optimize energy efficiency while maintaining Quality of Service (QoS). The proposed approach introduces a hierarchical O-RAN-aligned control framework in which a Non-Real-Time RAN Intelligent Controller (Non-RT RIC) periodically computes energy-aware policies from long-term historical data, while a Near-Real-Time RIC enforces those policies through per-User Equipment (UE) handover actions on a sub-second timescale. We formulate a joint energy- and QoS-aware load balancing problem as a Mixed-Integer Non-Linear Programming (MINLP) model. This model optimizes UE association across E2 Nodes to minimize transmission power and autonomously deactivate underutilized cells, while satisfying strict QoS constraints. To validate the proposed solution, we deploy it in an experimental environment that simulates massive sports events. Experimental results demonstrate 72% energy savings over a 24-hour trace and sub-second handover delays (0.123-0.204 s/UE), confirming the solution's feasibility for autonomous and sustainable 5G Advanced networks. This work provides guidelines for deploying energy-efficient strategies in O-RAN environments and underscores the potential of adaptive solutions for sustainable mobile communications.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management, 2026

item.title: ViTrail: Transmission-Inference Co-Design for Vision Transformer-Based Mobile Video Analytics
item.description: arXiv:2601.21362v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Edge-assisted mobile video analytics (MVA) relies on a tight device-edge feedback loop in which captured frames are transmitted for remote inference and the returned results are rendered on the mobile device. Many existing systems optimize frame transmission while treating server-side inference as a fixed cost. This separation becomes inefficient for vision transformer (ViT)-based dense prediction, where high-resolution inputs simultaneously increase network traffic and server computation. We present ViTrail, which co-designs transmission and ViT inference through a shared mixed-resolution representation. The device preserves task-relevant regions at full resolution and downsamples less informative regions before encoding. The server tokenizes each region at its transmitted resolution, so the same regional resolution assignment reduces both the upload payload and the number of tokens processed by the ViT. For dense prediction, ViTrail aligns regions with ViT patches and attention windows and restores a regular feature grid at a configurable stage. At runtime, it selects regional downsampling, compression quality, and the restoration point to maximize predicted installation accuracy, the accuracy of the rendered result when a new remote result is first used for rendering. We build a fully functional prototype on commodity mobile and edge devices and evaluate it in real time across 300 video-trace pairs with real-world 4G/5G traces. ViTrail achieves the highest mean rendering accuracy among the evaluated systems and leads each baseline on 81% to 95% of pairs, while reducing median end-to-end offloading latency by 38% against the most accurate baseline.
item.dc:creator: Miao Zhang, Guanzhen Wu, Hao Fang, Yifei Zhu, Fangxin Wang, Ruixiao Zhang, Linfeng Shen, Jiangchuan Liu

item.title: Pramana: A Composable, Domain-Specific Backend for Empirical Networking Research
item.description: arXiv:2607.26352v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Empirical networking research often tests a hypothesis with data the study itself generates, so accelerating this research requires shortening the time from forming a hypothesis to generating that data. Consider whether a bulk BBR download fairly shares its bottleneck with a Google Meet call. Testing this requires configuring a realistic bottleneck link, running the BBR transfer and the Meet call together, and collecting the call's quality metrics. Today a researcher builds this setup from scratch for each new idea; this delay from idea to data is the ideation-to-data gap. AI agents already propose hypotheses faster than researchers can generate data to test them. Closing the gap needs a backend that generates the data for each new hypothesis on demand, without a new setup. We envision Pramana, a composable backend for networking research designed as a thin waist, with research intents above it and execution substrates below. At its core, the intent specification separates the data a study needs (the intent) from where that data is generated (the substrate) and how it is produced (the mechanism), so one specification can target any substrate. We build a corpus of 255 data-generation intents from 66 published papers and find that the intent specification expresses all of them, while no existing tool covers more than 11%. Our proof-of-concept implementation covers 27% of these intents. For CCAnalyzer, one of the 66 papers, the implementation regenerated the data for one trial of each network setting and congestion-control algorithm in the paper's main experiment. We lay out what implementing the full design requires and why it needs a community effort.

item.title: When Weak Reports Matter: Staged Anchored Fusion for Cooperative UAV Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2610.07747v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An echo rejected locally may still help other receivers confirm a target. Staged anchored recovery (SAR) retains confirmations based on strong reports, then uses unused strong reports to retrieve compatible weak evidence. This retrieval preserves every remaining candidate containing a strong report once the initial associations are fixed. We derive sharp bounds on corroborating support when receivers have different evidence probabilities and arbitrary dependence, constructing a joint distribution that attains every value between the bounds. For advance source selection with nonnegative additive costs, any feasible worst-case true/false support constraints can be met optimally by querying no weak-report source or just one. Simulations of unmanned aerial vehicle sensing show additional recoveries over strict consensus, sometimes accompanied by more unmatched outputs. In further tests, recovered positions often lack full velocity estimates, shared reflections create false confirmations, and query overhead can exceed upload savings.
item.dc:creator: Xingqin Lin

item.title: AdaPTwin: Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Predictive Digital Twin for Proactive Radio Resource Management in Vehicular Networks
item.description: arXiv:2605.21897v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The highly dynamic nature of vehicular networks necessitates proactive and site-specific radio resource management (RRM) for safety-critical services. While Network Digital Twins (NDTs) have emerged as a promising enabler, physics-based ray tracing is time-consuming, challenging accurate RRM under strict latency constraints. We propose AdaPTwin, an adaptive multi-fidelity predictive NDT framework for proactive and latency-aware RRM in vehicular networks. Unlike single- and multi-fidelity NDTs with fixed fidelity levels, AdaPTwin selects the NDT fidelity by constrained optimization under a per-slot latency budget. The framework adopts a hierarchical cloud-edge architecture: fidelity selection is performed periodically in the cloud, whereas the proactive RRM loop runs at the edge in every slot. The edge loop predicts the channels between vehicles and roadside units (RSUs) through trajectory forecasting, using a Transformer with continual learning, and look-ahead ray tracing with NVIDIA Sionna over a dynamically updated 3D scene of buildings, roads, and vehicles. A joint RSU beamforming and vehicle-RSU association problem is then solved to maximize the proportionally fair sum rate using a scalable multi-start iterative coordinate descent algorithm. AdaPTwin is assessed in a simulation-based evaluation in which a high-fidelity reference NDT, rather than field measurements, provides the accuracy reference. Comparisons with reactive, single-fidelity, and non-adaptive predictive NDTs and the stochastic 3GPP model show that AdaPTwin adapts to the evaluated traffic densities and urban layouts, where fixed-fidelity DT frameworks either lose accuracy or overrun their deadline. In the evaluated scenarios, AdaPTwin achieves up to 70% sum-rate gain and 80% outage probability reduction compared with a non-adaptive predictive multi-fidelity NDT while meeting the per-slot deadline.
item.dc:creator: Armin Makvandi, Md. Zoheb Hassan, Md. Jahangir Hossain

item.title: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
item.description: arXiv:2610.28596v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times. When a Bell pair is generated, the qubits may need to be stored in memory while waiting for other links to succeed. Recently, new protocols have been proposed to reduce this storage overhead by processing and releasing some switch qubits before all Bell links are available. However, these protocols do not characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required at each stage. Moreover, the local-cover method in the state-of-the-art Piecemaker protocol is computationally expensive for general target graphs. In this work, we characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required after any subset of users' Bell links are generated and processed. We then develop an online stabilizer-transition protocol that attains this limit, which can be implemented in polynomial time in the number of qubits $n$ and does not require information about future Bell-link successes. Moreover, when one Bell link succeeds per round of duration $\Delta t$, for the path graph $P_n$, Piecemaker requires the cumulative switch-qubit storage time $\Theta(n^2\Delta t)$ and peak memory of at least $\left\lfloor n/2 \right\rfloor$ \textit{for any arrival order}, while under some arrival orders, our protocol requires only $(n-1)\Delta t$ and retains just one persistent switch qubit. More generally, for tree graphs, our protocol can reduce the $\Theta(n^2\Delta t)$ cumulative storage time in Piecemaker to $O(n\log n\,\Delta t)$ for some arrival orders.
item.dc:creator: Lei Hu, Alptug Aytekin, Stavros Mitrolaris, Mohamed Nomeir, Subhankar Banerjee, Sennur Ulukus, Saikat Guha
